chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Wahb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performed salat (prayer) while there was urine or janābah on his garment. He said: “Whether he knew of it or did not know, then he must repeat the salat (prayer) when he comes to know.”

His statement عليه السلام, “whether he knew of it or did not know,” means thereby his state at the time of rising for salat (prayer), after knowledge of the occurrence of impurity in the garment had already preceded that, yet at the time of rising for salat (prayer) he was unaware due to an occurrence of inadvertence or forgetfulness. But if no knowledge at all had previously preceded him regarding the occurrence of the impurity before that, then repeating the salat (prayer) would not have been obligatory upon him in any case, as indicated by the first report; otherwise, the reports would contradict one another.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever performs salat (prayer) in a usurped garment or in a usurped place, it does not suffice him, and repeating the salat (prayer) is obligatory upon him. That is indicated by what is undisputed, namely that salat (prayer) in both of them is prohibited, and prohibition indicates the invalidity of that which is prohibited, as has been explained elsewhere. Also, there is no disagreement that salat (prayer) requires the intention of nearness, and this salat (prayer) is reprehensible without disagreement, and seeking nearness through reprehensible acts is not valid under any circumstance.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat (prayer) due to invalidity or defect
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine as a source of ritual impurity
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state or trace of major ritual impurity requiring purification
key_terms.نِيَّةِ ٱلْقُرْبَةِ: intention of seeking nearness to Allah through worship
key_terms.ٱلنَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity present on the garment

ai.seo_question: Must salat (prayer) be repeated if someone discovers impurity on his garment afterward or prayed in a usurped place?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings about salat (prayer) performed in a garment affected by impurity and clarifies the distinction between prior knowledge, forgetfulness, and complete lack of awareness. It also states that salat (prayer) in a usurped garment or place is invalid and must be repeated because an act of worship requiring nearness to Allah cannot be valid when performed through what is prohibited.
